findings.body: This previous finding remains open. A failed check overrides the saved status without comparing the response's headRefOid with the local branch head. After a repair commit, tasks and fixes can therefore still show checks failed and advertise forge work instead of forge close, in both board and next output. Preserve the PR's check display, but apply the failure to local readiness only when it describes the current head.
findings.title: Ignore previous-head failures when deriving the local next step

findings.body: This previous finding remains open. The machine board queries only open PRs and passes an empty merged-PR set to the story calculation. A task or fix merged on GitHub can consequently retain its old stage and merge advice until origin/main is fetched. The unchanged next-step implementation already obtains merged branches at src/forge/nextstep.py:189 and uses them at lines 506–516. Share that evidence with machine task/fix stages and story next steps.
findings.title: Recognize GitHub merges before the default branch is fetched

findings.body: The live stage uses only the currently active run's start, resetting its timer when another attempt starts in the same round. Both Claude and Codex commit nudges launch a second run (src/forge/worker.py:193–199 and 212–219); review retries do likewise (src/forge/review.py:464–470). Earlier starts remain recorded but are excluded from live here. Build and Review therefore lose elapsed time during the second attempt, then jump to the full duration when timing is recorded. Anchor the stage clock to its first recorded start in the current round while retaining the active worker's own start.
findings.title: Preserve the live stage's start across attempts in one round
